draft.shortGloss: to try; to taste; to try on; to prove
draft.emotion: curious and eager, leaning in to see what something is like
notes: Stem-changing verb (o → ue): pruebo, pruebas, prueba, prueban.
Use 'probar' to try out a thing or experience; to try to do an action (+ infinitive), use 'intentar' or 'tratar de'.
For trying on clothes, use the reflexive form 'probarse'.

senses.definition: To test or use something to see if it works or if you like it.

examples.text: Voy a probar este nuevo método para estudiar.
examples.translation: I am going to try this new method for studying.

senses.definition: To eat or drink a small amount of something to check its flavor.

examples.text: Quiero probar la sopa para ver si tiene suficiente sal.
examples.translation: I want to taste the soup to see if it has enough salt.
examples.emotion: hungry and expectant, waiting for the first bite

senses.definition: (reflexive, probarse) To put on an item of clothing to see how it fits.

examples.text: Puedes probarte esta chamarra en el probador.
examples.translation: You can try on this jacket in the fitting room.

senses.definition: To show that something is true using evidence.

examples.text: No puedo probar que él dice la verdad.
examples.translation: I can't prove that he is telling the truth.
